title: The Wild Month of June 2024
excerpt: A Summer Break I won't forget for a long time
content:
## A Long Story Ahead
As I have told in a few of my previous posts, June 2024 was one hell of an experience in my life. Starting with a trip to a Water Park with college friends in temperatures reaching very close to 50 degrees, I did try beating some heat in the beginning, although what was to follow was certainly going to tepefy me for a month. I gave two more college exams after that trip to return home with a hint of uncertainty and anxiety. It was not that this anxiety had suddenly crept in, but it was a process in the making for quite some time. The previous summer, I was the first person in my entire college to secure an internship, but this time the tables had turned. A few of my friends and batchmates had secured good internships at startups and organizations (some of them in really great ones, too, and when I say really great, I mean it), and this time, I was left with nothing when I returned home. I used to constantly berate myself for wasting a year as head of the Placement Cell in college. In big colleges, you do get an advantage of being in the placement cell, but in a Tier 3 College, where companies hardly visit, it's not the case, especially if you are hit with a recession year. You get to do the stuff of marketing and call centre people of calling hundreds of HRs, trying to convince them to visit your college, so that at least one of them agrees, and you are assured that one company is added to your batch, too, possibly. Now the work is good, but what about the crucial time which got wasted due to this, where I could learn core CS concepts, do DSA problems, prepare good development projects or apply to internships for startups and do their assignments cause big companies certainly won't visit your college and in a recession year can't expect the resume to get shortlisted there too. But enough of the rant towards Placement Cell (where I literally was a part and was the head, but still I am cursing it), I know that some time definitely would remain every day but man I am a human and am not perfect with too many things on the plate, it becomes hard to focus on one. Ok, going back to the summer, I knew I had to roll out papads(convert that to Hindi to get the actual meaning).
So, I literally started to apply to every position possible, as in my mind it was clear that without another internship, getting a good full-time opportunity would be difficult, especially being from a tier 3 college. Now, an average tier 3 college guy can't rely on an internship only (unless you are exceptional, have done GSOC and all, or are a Master on CF). You have to continue building projects that are better than the previous ones, continuously grind on DSA, and maybe give contests on LC/CF, and appear for initial rounds of hackathons, just to get that chance of having something, and I repeat at least something to show on your resume. Anyway, your resume is already gonna be rejected just by reading your college name and dumped to a spam folder most probably, XD. But we used to prepare for that 1% of the cases where someone notices your resume and maybe thinks, let's give him a shot. And this is possible only if you have shot multiple arrows at different places to expect at least one to hit the target (in our case, a placement).
So, I used to just start my day by opening various platforms for around 30 minutes, like Cuvette, Internshala, WellFound, LinkedIn, etc., to apply for matching roles. Then I used to try the Problem of the Day on GFG and LeetCode, respectively. Initially, I would try to solve them for quite some time, but later I used to apply a timer of 30, 45, and 60 minutes for easy, medium, and hard problems, respectively. If I wasn't able to solve that problem in these times, then I used to watch the solution to the Problem on YouTube on Channels like Neetcode and Aryan Mittal. Now, this solution checking may sound bad, but that was the necessity given the limited time you have for placement preparation. Apart from this, if it were a Sunday and I woke up in time, then I would also try to give the Weekly contest on LeetCode. Well, mornings were kind of very planned and reserved for this DSA and stuff. But the rest of the day was absolute chaos. I used to juggle between learning some new development concept and applying that from YouTube (mostly Harkirat), or work on a new project, or try to collaborate with my teammates to make anything for a hackathon (even a presentation), or work on the assignment projects given by startups for an internship, or solve Striver's sheet. All this while constantly having a look at every email I receive to keep an eye on if I haven't missed an update about a follow-up to any opportunity I applied to, if I received any. Most of the time, these follow-ups turned out to be rejection mails, very unsurprisingly. All this while hearing stories of your friends about how awesome their intern work is, or seeing their Insta stories of them chilling. It was a great decision to discontinue Instagram back then for a while. I only remember chilling that month for once when I went to watch the re-release of Rockstar with my brother, a commitment I had made with him, since he was missing out on all the fun and outings I was having in hostel life (which everybody has). I remember that Stir who's interview experience I have already shared (what are you doing if you haven't read that yet), had it's interview scheduled on the same day of when our tickets were booked so I asked the founder to reschedule for one day earlier (so that I don't disappoint my brother also) while also showing keen interest for the role. That turned out to be a rejection anyway.
I even remember that while the India vs Australia T20 WC Match was going on, where Rohit Sharma played that iconic knock, while watching the match, I was making an assignment for a role which I continued making till the morning, so that the theory of the earlier you submit, the better your chances are applied. I did the same during the Final Match, too, while also preparing for Graviti's interview, which was scheduled quite close to that date. I had flashbacks of the final 2 or 3 overs even during the interview, but I controlled myself there. This cycle continued for the entire month of June and the first three days of July. I received OAs from many companies, tried to give contests on LC / CF from time to time, made multiple assignments, sat for 4-5 interviews, and all this while constantly facing rejection on my applications. It was depressing mostly, but with Spotify on for the entire day with the food at home (which I am missing these days in Bangalore), I started to live with it.
The good thing that turned out from these 30 days was that I finally got interview calls, the one thing I had missed for a year since being selected for Blockstash. Mostly this was due to being tired and all from placement cell work that I couldn't devote myself wholly to all this, but at home I got myself locked in and had a really stark difference in results than before, and it even provided me a selection in Graviti. It was a crucial thing for me to sit for interviews to get that important experience of interviews, so that I don't get nervous in the placement season and for the entire year or so. Striver's SDE Sheet questions were also given an opportunity to be tested upon me although I am not really proud of my progress in DSA this month, mostly due to being busy with assignments and startup selection-focused work. Now, some might say that this is not enough; there are so many success stories of people cracking so many opportunities, but chill man, I too have a life, and I admire those who can find success by devoting themselves to the Tech world. But this is my story of the time that anxiety and FOMO provided a very important outcome to me.
It seems I wrote a lot of crap on this one, which I don't regret because it all happened with me, trust me.
author: Akshat
